messages:
tara: Quick heads-up — canary from last night shows a small but consistent uptick in hallucination rate for FP8 paths on short Q&A prompts (~1-3 tokens answers). Not huge, but reproducible in ~0.4% of traces.
max: Oof. Seen any stratification by model or input length?
tara: Mostly appears for shorter answers where the model compresses context. Happens on both model-a and model-b variants, more frequent on model-b.
olivia: Are these traces coming from dedicated or hosted?
tara: Hosted, mixed regions. We routed traffic through precision-lanes: fp8-primary -> int8-fallback if degscore>0.2. But we only measured token-level degscore afterwards.
max: Can you paste the routing config?
tara: Sure — snippet from deploy config: ```
precision_routing:
  - name: fast_lowbit
    preferred: [fp8, int8]
    deg_threshold: 0.2
    max_latency_ms: 40
```
matt: Those thresholds look fine-ish. My suspicion: fp8 path is fine for long-form, but a headwise saturation edge for short answers makes logits sharper in certain heads -> overconfident wrong tokens.
leila: We discussed headwise saturation last quarter. We never surfaced a signal in runtime for "head saturation" specifically. We mostly have token-level entropy / degscore.
max: Could we add a cheap runtime metric: headwise_snr or topk-gap per-token? Even a 1-2 value per request that flags extreme head concentration could help routing.
olivia: +1. That would let the router consider quality not just degscore. Could do a small post-softmax pass on the last layer. Low overhead if we sample 1 token.
leila: I propose adding a "quality_severity" tag to telemetry that aggregates: {degscore, entropy, head_gap}. Router can then use a weighted policy.
max: Love it. We should also decide if router should *prefer* int8 proactively for requests with short prompt length or only react when quality flag is high.
matt: Proactive rule seems safer: short_prompt && fp8 && head_gap>0.15 -> route to int8. Reactive rule requires doing fp8 first then falling back, which costs latency and might still cause bad output visible to user.
leila: Agreed. We likely want an optimistic fast path only when short_prompt and no head_gap risk. For short prompts we should bias toward int8 if we lack a strong quality signal.
max: Telemetry change plan: add head_gap (float), head_gap_counted (bool), sample_token_index. Also add route_decision_reason enum.
leila: Example route config idea: ```
routing_v2:
  policies:
    - name: short_prompt_safe
      match: "prompt_len <= 80"
      prefer: [int8, fp8]
      quality_bypass: false
    - name: long_prompt_perf
      match: "prompt_len > 80"
      prefer: [fp8, int8]
      quality_bypass: true
```
max: Nice. Ops concern: telemetry volume increases. We should sample telemetry for production (1-5%) but fully log canaries.
srebot: incidentbot: Canary alert created: CAN-2026-0921-fp8-short-qna. Link: https://incidents.redwood/canary/CAN-2026-0921-fp8-short-qna
tara: Action items: 1) add head_gap telemetry (leila) 2) routing_v2 prototype (max) 3) canary replay and targeted shadow (olivia) 4) ops sampling plan (matt). Owners assigned.
leila: I'll draft telemetry schema and a short perf budget. Will include expected overhead numbers.
max: I'll prototype router changes and wire the reason enum. Will also add a small unit test simulating saturated heads.
olivia: I'll run a focused shadow run for the last 48h traffic slice and replay the failing traces.
matt: Ops will do sampling rollout and watch cost. I'll add an alert if head_gap sampling rate >1% among short prompts.
tara: Cool. If we get quick wins we can bake config into dedicated clusters as a safe default.
max: One more: add a synthetic test in the canary suite that fuzzes short Q&A and checks for hallucination regression >0.2%. Easy to automate.
leila: Noted. I'll sync with QA.
tara: Thanks all :thumbsup:
max: Thanks — will post PRs to infra + runtime tomorrow.
